oneStopSecurity.note: Fraport: whether a connecting passenger is screened depends on the origin. EU one-stop security (Reg. 2015/1998 Attachment 4-B as amended by Reg. 2019/413 and 2025/920): passengers from EU / EEA / Swiss airports and from the recognised third countries are not re-screened on transfer. Ben Gurion (TLV) was removed by Reg. 2025/920, Kangerlussuaq, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey too. Belgrade (BEG) was added by Reg. 2020/111 and not removed since (consolidated text reconstructed from mirrors, likely: docs/research/EVIDENCE_2026-11-02.md); Reg. 2025/920 applies from 21 May 2025. The official consolidated Attachment 4-B was not read (EUR-Lex: owner capture).

specialScreening.text: Tel Aviv departures (Lufthansa, El Al, Condor) board at Terminal 1 concourse C: all 13 TLV departures with a gate in the feed (2026-10-30 – 11-01) used C4 or C6; El Al checks in at Hall C (Fraport). No official Fraport text on additional screening for Israel flights was found, so its time is not known.

Lufthansa to the USA: the required USA entry-data verification is done at check-in / Fast Bag Drop (biometric consent online). Gate-level US measures (TSA 2017 enhanced screening) are not public: time not known.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

lines.name: Sky Line (new line) · public car

service.notes: Official: every 2–3 min, 04:00–23:00 (orientation and T3 pages, read 2026-10-31). Since the 15 June 2026 restart Fraport pauses the Sky Line every night 23:00–04:00 "until further notice" (inspections by Siemens Mobility; shuttle buses instead) and runs up to 8 vehicles at max. 50 km/h. Wait = half the headway.

lines.eligibility: Everyone, free of charge (public car: Schengen passengers, origin/destination passengers, visitors, staff). Luggage carts not allowed.
lines.notes: 5.6 km; official "eight minutes or less" T1–T3 incl. the T2 stop (Fraport fact sheet), hessenschau and Meilenoptimieren 8–10 min, OMAAT/InsideFlyer "roughly 10 minutes". Measured T3 → T1 (Travel & Walk for you, published 23 Jun 2026, after the restart at 50 km/h): leaves T3 ≈140 s, stops at T2 ≈400–410 s, arrives at T1 ≈555 s → ≈4.3 + 0.2 + 2.4 ≈ 6.9 min door to door. Ride segments are therefore measured; the 4 → 6 min range on T2–T3 covers the reported 8–10 min totals. Each two-car vehicle is divided into a public (Schengen/landside) part and a non-Schengen transfer part (fact sheet).

status.note: Opened to the public with Terminal 3 on 23 April 2026.
New Sky Line out of service after recurring technical faults; replacement shuttle buses between the terminals. Restarted 15 June 2026 with up to 8 vehicles at max. 50 km/h.

rules.text: Terminal 2 (piers D and E) has been closed to passengers since 9 June 2026 for a multi-year refurbishment (reopening planned mid-2030s). All former T2 airlines moved to Terminal 3 in four waves (23 Apr, 5 May, 19 May, 9 Jun 2026). The T2 Sky Line station stays in use as interchange.

New Sky Line in 2026: opened with T3 on 23 April; suspended 28 May – 14 June after recurring technical faults (replacement shuttle buses between the terminals, every 2 min by day and every 10 min at night per Wikipedia); restarted 15 June with up to 8 vehicles at max. 50 km/h; paused every night 23:00–04:00 until further notice, with shuttle buses instead. No later suspension found in news up to October 2026.

During the 28 May – 14 June 2026 suspension of the new Sky Line, Fraport ran landside shuttle buses (up to 20 buses, every 2–3 min by day and every 10 min 23:00–05:00, stops at the arrival forecourts) and a separate airside shuttle with up to five buses between the terminals for transfer passengers; the existing T1–T2 Sky Line stayed in operation. The airside buses are not routed (stops not published).

Terminal 3 (piers G, H, J) opened on 23 April 2026 (ceremony 22 April). Pier H = Schengen (10 jet-bridge positions + 5 bus gates), pier J = non-Schengen (14 jet-bridge positions + 8 bus gates, separate arrivals level 2), pier G = 14 near-building bus gates, Schengen and non-Schengen capable, initially only partly used. Lufthansa Group and Star Alliance stay in Terminal 1; Condor moves to T3 in 2027.

Terminal 1 separates Schengen and non-Schengen by level and pier section: A (level 2) Schengen and Z (level 3, same stands) non-Schengen; B1–B19 Schengen and B20–B63 non-Schengen; C non-Schengen. Some B bus gates carry two numbers (B14–B16 Schengen = B60–B62 non-Schengen).

T1 ↔ T3: the free Sky Line runs 04:00–23:00 every 2–3 min (≈8–10 min T1–T3 via T2); shuttle buses run at night (official 22:00–05:00; Sky Line pause 23:00–04:00). Each Sky Line train has a public car and a car reserved for non-Schengen transfer passengers; airside non-Schengen passengers from T1 reach it by the old SkyLine to T2, and at T3 it serves the pier J arrivals level. Schengen passengers change landside and pass security again in T3. Airside non-Schengen T1 ↔ T3 transfers change from the old SkyLine to the new line at T2 (JAL; Loungerocker video).

Fraport: transfer passengers may have to pass a security check again; Short Transfer Lanes exist at most border and security checkpoints in Terminal 1. T3 uses CT scanners (liquids up to 2 l per container may stay in the bag in T3).

Lufthansa minimum connecting time at FRA: 60 min since the summer 2025 schedule (previously 45 min; no split by Schengen status or terminal reported). Guides advise 75–120 min for T1 ↔ T3 connections; Fraport says ~45 min T1 ↔ T3 transfers are achievable. JAL publishes MCT 90 min for T3 → T1 and 55 min for T3 → T3 (search excerpt of its transit page). No Fraport-published MCT table was found.

Baggage on connections (Fraport): "In most cases, your checked baggage will be automatically checked through to your destination airport." Otherwise passengers collect it at baggage reclaim and check it in again with the airline; this also applies to separately booked connections (self-transfer), which therefore leave through entry control and reclaim and re-enter through check-in and security. The model has no baggage-reclaim or re-check-in time; customs handling of checked-through bags on a non-Schengen → Schengen/domestic connection is not established from an official source (q:fra-customs-transfer).

Transfer checkpoints in Fraport's waiting-time data (via Qsensor, read 2026-11-01). T1: Hall A L2 transfer passport control (into A, A1–A69); Hall A L4 transfer security checkpoint (A/Z, Z11–Z69); Hall B L3 transfer security checkpoint (B non-Schengen, B20–B63). T3: Hall J L3 transfer security checkpoint (G, H, J); Hall H L3 transfer passport control (to J); Hall J L3 transfer passport control (to H). No transfer checkpoint is listed for concourse C. Whether a connecting passenger is screened depends on the origin (EU one-stop security); opening hours are not published.
